rules: Saving writes each source's comments first, then writes a source only if it is fully writable (otherwise reported as "not writable"), then remembers the chosen source types and locations for the next start. The person sees "Success." with the user and computer outcomes, or "Saving failed!" with the reason. (PolicyPlus/Main.vb:625)

The computer counts as having the Group Policy infrastructure only when the number Windows gives for its edition equals one of 59 fixed codes in a list. The edition is asked for as Windows version 6.0, and the result of the call is not checked. When the call fails the edition stays 0, which is not in the list, so the computer counts as having none. (PolicyPlus/SystemInfo.vb:3)
A policy file is refused when it does not start with the 'PReg' signature, with the message 'Missing PReg signature'. (PolicyPlus/PolicySource.vb:33)
A policy file is refused when its format version is not 1, with the message 'Unknown (newer) version of POL format'. (PolicyPlus/PolicySource.vb:34)

When comments are saved, each comment gets its own text id built from the policy's namespace, policy name and a running number, and each distinct namespace gets a prefix made from its name (dots turned into underscores) and the running number. (PolicyPlus/CmtxFile.vb:50)
When a policy file is read, an extra empty character after the value name, as Microsoft's documentation allows, is skipped. (PolicyPlus/PolicySource.vb:50)

When a policy file is read and the same key and value name occur twice, the later entry wins. Key and value names are matched without regard to letter case, and the first spelling seen is kept for saving. (PolicyPlus/PolicySource.vb:59)
When a policy file is saved, entries are written in alphabetical order, so a key-clearing marker is always written before the values it clears. (PolicyPlus/PolicySource.vb:77)
unconfirmed: For the capability: The Group Policy check relies on a fixed list of edition codes. We assume those codes are the professional, enterprise, education and server editions, and that Home editions are absent. The code names no editions. If wrong: The program would hide or show its warning about missing Group Policy on the wrong computers.
